message.abstract: <jats:p>Background/Objectives: Multimodal deep learning for glaucoma detection often combines fundus imaging with optical coherence tomography (OCT), yet it is unclear when fusion adds information beyond OCT alone and how such models behave under domain shift. We compared joint and late fusion of scanning laser ophthalmoscopy (SLO) and OCT and their cross-domain transfer. Methods: Models trained on GAMMA (color fundus photographs and macular OCT; 99 cases) were applied without retraining to the Harvard-FairVision glaucoma test split (3000 patients; SLO and OCT). Unimodal and multimodal models were then trained on FairVision (6000 training and 1000 validation patients). Four candidates (OCT-only, concatenation and cross-attention fusion, and late fusion with a cross-fitted SLO weight of 0.15) were locked with their calibration and thresholds and evaluated once on the same test split. Results: Cross-domain transfer yielded areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROCs) of 0.635–0.653. In-domain OCT-only reached a test AUROC of 0.876. Neither jointly trained cross-attention fusion (ΔAUROC −0.0045; 95% confidence interval (CI) −0.0110 to 0.0021) nor concatenation fusion (+0.0009; 95% CI −0.0056 to 0.0074) improved on OCT-only. Late fusion yielded a small ranking improvement (+0.0059; 95% CI 0.0033 to 0.0087; Holm-adjusted p = 0.0012), but a sensitivity gain at matched specificity was not established. Post hoc analyses identified lower AUROC among Black patients and a higher false-positive rate among normal eyes. Conclusions: OCT carried most of the diagnostic information. Standard joint fusion did not add value. Low-weight late fusion improved ranking slightly on a previously accessed test split; this requires independent confirmation and does not establish clinical benefit. Fusion claims require strong unimodal and late-fusion baselines and external validation.</jats:p>
title: When Does Multimodal Fusion Help? Cross-Domain Transfer, Joint Fusion, and Late Fusion of SLO and OCT for Glaucoma Detection Under an Analysis-Locked Evaluation
